structure:
Part 5: animals e2e/features, accompanying documents and promoted notifications. Read in full: the 11 flat specs tests/animals/e2e/features/documents-entry.spec.ts (24 lines), documents-save-buttons.spec.ts (104), documents-limits.spec.ts (69), documents-reject.spec.ts (24), documents-scan-lifecycle.spec.ts (83), documents-two-tabs.spec.ts (67), documents-back-button.spec.ts (38), documents-refresh-no-js.spec.ts (53), documents-large-uploads.spec.ts (37), promoted-documents.spec.ts (62) and promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts (97); and as support context page-objects/animals/accompanying-documents-page.ts, notification-view-page.ts and overview-page.ts, page-objects/shared/base-page.ts, view-header.ts and govuk-banners.ts, domain/animals/constants/document-types.ts, domain/animals/types/accompanying-document.ts, domain/animals/models/db/accompanying-document.ts, flows/animals/journey.ts and notification-actions.ts, fixtures/ui.ts, utils/eicar-upload.ts, synthetic-file-writer.ts and scan-status.ts, config/file-upload-timeouts.ts and every file under resources/file-upload. Also read, for the meaning of the tags these specs carry, the tag paragraphs of the repo README (@duplicated-in-frontend, @compose, @cross-browser) and, for support values the specs reach through, page-objects/shared/sets.ts, page-objects/shared/date-picker.ts, domain/animals/constants/journey-options.ts (the document answers) and domain/animals/models/api/notification-status.ts.

The nine documents-*.spec.ts files hold 17 literal test() declarations, which run as 27 tests because documents-save-buttons.spec.ts (5 declarations, one of them inside a loop over the three save buttons) and documents-back-button.spec.ts (1 declaration) are each wrapped in a loop over 'with JavaScript' and 'without JavaScript'. promoted-documents.spec.ts holds 3 and promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts 4. The partition's covers line states 40, 6 and 8 for these three groups; the files on disk hold the counts above, and every test in all 11 files has a claim here.

Covered: the Upload documents page (its route and entry from the Overview task list, its heading, every field with its label and component, the three save buttons and the added-documents table with all five columns and its two row actions); every validation and refusal message these specs prove verbatim; the 15-document cap and the 50MB file-size cap with its exact-boundary and one-byte-over cases; the whole virus-scan lifecycle (pending, clean, infected) with the wording each state shows and what the review page says about a rejected document; what each save button lands on; the no-JavaScript paths (the refresh fallback, the browser back button, two tabs); the promoted-notification document integration (download headers, byte fidelity, removal); and the notification lifecycle statuses promoted-lifecycle.spec.ts drives through the backend API. Gaps recorded where the constants and helpers in scope name a document type, file type, limit, status or stored field that no test in this slice asserts.

claims.statement: A trader opens the documents page from the notification Overview by following a task link named "Upload documents", and it is reachable with only the country of origin answered.
The documents page's level-1 heading is "Upload documents".
The documents page's address is /live-animals/notifications/<reference number>/accompanying-documents.
claims.note: The slug, the set base and the URL template are each stated; the full address follows from the three together.

claims.statement: The shared route every documents spec takes to the page saves the origin, answers the commodity, then opens the Overview task "Upload documents", so the page is reached mid-journey rather than as the first page.
The documents page asks for a document reference in a field labelled "Document reference".
The documents page asks for the document type in a select labelled "Document type".
The document type select opens with no type chosen, on an option reading "Select one".

After "Select one" the document type select offers thirteen types in this exact order: ITAHC (Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate); Other veterinary certificate / veterinary declaration; Self-declaration; Journey log; Import permit / authorisation; CITES permit/certificate; Air waybill; Sea waybill; Rail waybill; Bill of lading; Commercial invoice; Packing list / species list; Other supporting documents.
claims.quote:
export const ITAHC_DOCUMENT_TYPE_LABEL = 'ITAHC (Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate)';

export const OFFERED_DOCUMENT_TYPE_LABELS = [
  ITAHC_DOCUMENT_TYPE_LABEL,
  'Other veterinary certificate / veterinary declaration',
  'Self-declaration',
  'Journey log',
  'Import permit / authorisation',
  'CITES permit/certificate',
  'Air waybill',
  'Sea waybill',
  'Rail waybill',
  'Bill of lading',
  'Commercial invoice',
  'Packing list / species list',
  'Other supporting documents',
];
claims.note: The test title names the count: 'the document type select opens on Select one, then offers thirteen document types in order'.

claims.statement: The documents page asks for a date of issue in a field named accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue, which the suite fills as a dd/mm/yyyy string such as 03/01/2026.
The date of issue is a Ministry of Justice date picker: the field sits inside a .moj-datepicker with a "Choose date" toggle button that opens a dialog.
claims.note: The page object declares the picker for this field, so the component is on the page; no test in this part opens it, so the picker's own behaviour is unproven here.

claims.statement: The documents page carries a file input for the document itself.
The documents page ends with three save controls: "Save and add another", "Save and continue" and "Save and return to overview".
The documents the trader has added are listed in a region named "File upload" holding a table named "Documents you have added".
With no document added, the File upload region holds no table: its text ends at "Save and add another".
An added document is listed under five column headings, in this order: Document reference, Document type, Date of issue, Status, Action.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments.addedDocumentsTable.getByRole('columnheader')).toHaveText([
      'Document reference',
      'Document type',
      'Date of issue',
      'Status',
      'Action',
    ]);

claims.statement: A document row's last cell holds both a link named "View file for document <position>" and a button named "Remove document <position>".
Saving a document with only the reference typed keeps the trader on the documents page and shows three errors, in this order: "Select a document type", "Enter a date of issue", "Upload a document".
All three save controls refuse a part-filled document the same way, and each keeps the reference the trader typed and adds no document.

Saving a document with a reference, a date of issue and an attached file but no document type shows exactly one error, "Select a document type", keeps the reference and the date of issue, and adds no document.
"Save and return to overview" on a document with every detail filled in lands on Overview, and reopening the Upload documents task lists that document.
"Save and return to overview" on an untouched documents form lands on Overview without an error and adds no document.
claims.note: So uploading a document is optional: an empty documents page may be left without an error.

claims.statement: "Save and continue" on an untouched documents form moves on to the Consignment addresses page.
Every save-button behaviour on the documents page is proven twice, once with JavaScript on and once with it off, so the page works without client JavaScript.
The documents page accepts at most fifteen documents.
Adding the fifteenth document raises no error summary: the cap is reached cleanly.
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments.errorSummary).toHaveCount(0);

claims.statement: Once fifteen documents are added the "Save and add another" control stays visible but is shut: it carries aria-disabled="true", is described by the element with id add-document-error, and has no formaction, so a sixteenth file is never sent.
claims.note: The spec's own comment states the reason: "The control keeps its place in the tab order so the error summary can reach it, so it is still on the page — but shut, and carrying no formaction, so a sixteenth file is never sent to be scanned and stored only to be turned away by the claim."

claims.statement: At the cap, the reason shown beside the add control reads "Error: You can upload a maximum of 15 files".
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments.addDocumentRefusedReason).toHaveText(`Error: ${maximumDocumentsMessage}`);

claims.statement: The largest file a document may be is 50MB, counted as 50,000,000 decimal bytes rather than 52,428,800 binary ones.
A PDF of exactly 50,000,000 bytes is accepted, scanned and listed as "Check completed", with no error summary.

A file one byte over 50,000,000 is refused: the page shows the "There is a problem" error summary with a link reading "The selected file must be smaller than 50MB", the file field's own error reads "Error: The selected file must be smaller than 50MB", and no document is added for it.
claims.note: Refusing the sixteenth file leaves the fifteen already added untouched: the row count stays at the one document added before it.

claims.statement: A clearly oversize file, 50.2MB, is refused with the same "The selected file must be smaller than 50MB" message whether the browser turns the pick away or the upload service refuses it on receipt, and no document is added.
A document of exactly the 50MB limit is stored whole: its View file link answers 200 and serves back bytes identical to the file uploaded, of the same length.
An unsupported file type, a .txt file, is refused: the page shows the "There is a problem" error summary, no document is added and the File upload region returns to its empty state.
No test in this slice asserts the wording of the message shown when a file's type is refused: only the error summary heading "There is a problem" is checked.
claims.note: Looked in promoted-documents.spec.ts (the only unsupported-type test in this part) and in resources/file-upload/constants.ts, which holds a message only for the size limit.

claims.statement: A document row shows one of three scan states: "Scanning for virus" while the check runs, "Check completed" when the file is clean, and "Virus found" when it is not.
While a document is still being scanned its row offers no "View file" link; the link appears only once the check has finished.
An infected upload settles to "Virus found" and the page shows the "There is a problem" error summary with the message "<file name> cannot be used. Remove it and try again with a different file."
claims.note: The file name in the message is the name the trader uploaded; the test drives it with the standard EICAR anti-virus test file named eicar-virus-file.pdf.

claims.statement: A document the scan has rejected offers no "View file" link at all.
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments.viewFile(1)).toHaveCount(0);

claims.statement: While a rejected document is still listed, "Save and continue" does not move the trader on: the same infected-file error is shown again.
claims.quote:
await animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments.saveAndContinue.click();
    await expect(infectedFileError).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: Removing the rejected document unblocks the journey: "Save and continue" then reaches the Consignment addresses page.
On the notification review, a rejected document's "Document 1" summary card reads "One or more of your documents were rejected. Return to Documents to remove and re-upload."
The review's error summary link for a rejected document points at that document's own card, by the card's element id.

A clean upload lists a Remove button straight away, lets "Save and return to overview" reach the Overview, and on reopening the Upload documents task the row reads "Check completed" with a View file link.
A virus scan is allowed up to 90 seconds to finish, sized for the real scanner in the deployed environment, which takes about 30 seconds on the EICAR file.

A small file's scan can finish before the page that follows the upload is drawn, so the "Scanning for virus" state is not guaranteed to be seen; the suite checks the pending wording only when it is still pending and records in the run report when the scanner won.
claims.quote:
/**
 * Waits for a document row to show its first scan status and reports whether
 * that status is still pending. A real scanner can settle a small file before
 * the redirected page renders, so the pending state is not guaranteed; the
 * local upload stub holds it until a refresh read. Run pending-state checks
 * only when `pending` is true. The run's report records when the scanner won.
 */
claims.note: mechanism: decides whether a pending-state assertion runs, from the text already in the document row; it is test scaffolding, not service behaviour.

claims.statement: Without client JavaScript, a document still being scanned shows a "Refresh" link, and that link's address carries attempt=1 on the first try.
Following the Refresh link re-reads the scan status, and repeating it eventually shows "Check completed" without any client JavaScript.
Once the scan has finished, the Refresh link is gone from the page and the document's View file link is shown instead.
The no-JavaScript refresh fallback is the one documents behaviour marked for the cross-browser run, so it is proven on browsers beyond the default one.
claims.quote:
test(
    'the refresh fallback reflects scan progress without client JavaScript',
    { tag: '@cross-browser' },

claims.statement: The no-JavaScript refresh test reaches the documents page by answering the origin with country FR and "No" to the region-code question, then the commodity, rather than through the shared route.
claims.note: Shows the origin page's own fields work without JavaScript too: a country select labelled "Country of origin" and a Yes/No radio.

claims.statement: A trader who leaves the documents page and returns to it with the browser back button can still add a second document; both documents are then listed, two rows in all.
Each time the documents page is drawn, the add control's upload address is a fresh one: after the back button the formaction differs from the one the first visit carried.
claims.note: A one-use upload address per page render; the back button serves a stale page and the service must hand it a new one before the next upload.

claims.statement: The back-button behaviour on the documents page is proven both with and without JavaScript.

Two browser tabs open on the same notification's documents page can each add their own document at the same time: both uploads settle to "Check completed", and after a refresh both rows are listed, two in all.
Neither tab's document serves the other tab's file: each row's View file link answers 200 with exactly the bytes that tab uploaded.
claims.note: The two files are given different lengths (2,000 and 3,000 bytes) precisely so that serving the wrong one fails the comparison.

claims.statement: A document's View file link serves the file as application/pdf with the x-content-type-options: nosniff header, answering 200, and the bytes match the file uploaded exactly.
Removing the only document empties the list: the row goes, the table goes, and the File upload region returns to its empty wording.
The document the download and listing tests add is of type VETERINARY_HEALTH_CERTIFICATE dated 03/01/2026, so a second document type beyond ITAHC is exercised end to end.
claims.note: ITAHC is the default the page object picks when a test names no type (accompanying-documents-page.ts:111-116).

claims.statement: The document download, listing and unsupported-type tests run only against the local compose stack, not in the default deployed-environment run, because they carry the @compose tag.
claims.quote:
test.describe('Promoted accompanying documents integration', { tag: '@compose' }, () => {
…
| `npm test`                                    | E2E suite, excluding `@compose` and `@a11y`            | CDP                  |
…
| `npm run test:docker-compose`                 | E2E + E2E integration (`@compose`) test suites         | docker-compose stack |

claims.statement: The spec titled "Promoted accompanying documents integration" exercises a draft notification, not a submitted one: it reaches the documents page through the ordinary draft route.
claims.note: toAccompanyingDocuments starts a new notification and never submits it, so nothing in this spec proves what a submitted notification's documents allow.

claims.statement: What a submitted notification's documents allow and refuse — whether a document can be added, removed or re-uploaded once the notification has been submitted — is not proven anywhere in this slice.
claims.note: Looked in both promoted-*.spec.ts files: the first works a draft, and the second only asserts that a submitted view shows no Change links and that an amendment opens at the review page.

claims.statement: A notification has four statuses: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED.
A newly created notification is DRAFT, and reading its fulfilments back reports the same reference number, the DRAFT status and an empty fulfilments list when it was created without one.
claims.note: A notification submitted without an ITAHC is allowed: the test's title names that case and no refusal follows.

claims.statement: Submitting a draft moves it to SUBMITTED, and its fulfilments read back reports SUBMITTED too.
claims.note: Submitting takes the notification's concurrency token, so a stale copy cannot submit it.

claims.statement: Amending a submitted notification moves it to AMEND, and its fulfilments read back reports AMEND.
Cancelling an amendment returns the notification to SUBMITTED.
claims.quote:
const cancelled = await notificationApi.cancelAmendNotification(id);
    expect(cancelled.status).toBe(notificationStatuses.submitted);

claims.statement: Copying a submitted notification twice produces two new notifications, each with its own reference number different from the original's and from each other's, and each starting as DRAFT.
claims.note: Both copies are taken with the same concurrency token, so copying does not consume it.

claims.statement: Deleting a notification moves it to DELETED, and deleting it again leaves it DELETED rather than failing.
A submitted notification's view is read-only: its heading is the notification reference, its status tag reads "Submitted", and the page offers no "Change" link.
A notification reference takes the form GBN-<letters>-<two digits>-<six letters or digits>, and it is the view's level-1 heading.
Amending a submitted notification from the dashboard opens a page headed "Review your notification" whose status tag reads "Amend".
Amend is reached from the notification list: the trader opens the dashboard, searches for the reference and follows the Amend action on that notification.
"Back" on a submitted notification's view, opened from the notification list, returns to the notification list.
"Back" on an amendment review opened by the Amend action returns to the dashboard.
The back link on a notification view is a link named exactly "Back", not a button.
The notification lifecycle tests also run only on the local compose stack, carrying the @compose tag.
claims.quote: test.describe('Notification lifecycle', { tag: '@compose' }, () => {

claims.statement: Six of the nine documents specs are marked as behaviour the frontend's own in-process suite also proves, so the same checks exist in two places: entry, save buttons, limits, rejection, the scan lifecycle and the no-JavaScript refresh.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/documents-entry.spec.ts:4, documents-limits.spec.ts:11, documents-reject.spec.ts:6, documents-scan-lifecycle.spec.ts:8, documents-refresh-no-js.spec.ts:8, README.md line 381
claims.note: documents-save-buttons.spec.ts carries no tag on its describe blocks; the tagged files are entry, limits, reject, scan-lifecycle and refresh-no-js. Two tabs, back button and large uploads are untagged, so only the end-to-end suite proves them.

claims.statement: Adding fifteen documents one after another is allowed two minutes, and the uploads and scans in these specs are each given three times the ordinary test budget.

A document a trader has added is stored with an upload id, a correlation id, its type, reference and date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD string, a scan status, and for each file its filename, declared and detected content types, length, storage key and bucket, file status and SHA-256 checksum.
claims.note: The date the trader types is dd/mm/yyyy but it is stored as YYYY-MM-DD, so the page and the store use different date formats.

claims.statement: No test in this slice reads a stored document record, so none of the stored fields — the scan status, the detected content type, the checksum or the storage key — is proven against what the page shows.
claims.note: Looked for the model's use across the 11 specs in this part: none of them imports it or touches the database.

claims.statement: A document a trader answers with is a file, optionally with a type, a reference and a date of issue, so all three details are optional in the shape the suite passes around even though the page refuses a save without them.
claims.note: mechanism: the test-side shape of a document answer; the page's own rules are the three required-field errors in repo-tests-p5-017.

claims.statement: Only two of the thirteen offered document types have a value any test can select: ITAHC and VETERINARY_HEALTH_CERTIFICATE. The other eleven labels are asserted as options but never chosen.
claims.note: So nothing in this slice proves that choosing, say, "Journey log" or "CITES permit/certificate" saves and lists correctly.

claims.statement: Which file types a document may be is not proven: the suite keeps safe .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .jpg and .jpeg fixtures, but every accepted upload in this slice is a PDF, and the only refusal proven is a .txt file.
claims.quote:
export const fileUploadPaths = {
  safeFile19kbDoc,
  safeFile10kbDocx,
  safeFile25kbXls,
  safeFile50kbXlsx,
  safeFile1kbPdf,
  safeFile100kbJpg,
  safeFile500kbJpeg,
  safeFile250bPng,
  restrictedFile10bTxt,
} as const;
claims.note: Every upload in the 11 specs uses safeFile1kbPdf, a PDF padded to size by writePaddedPdf, the EICAR PDF, a zero-filled .pdf, or restrictedFile10bTxt.

claims.statement: The suite names a 250-byte PNG upload fixture that the resources folder does not hold, so no test can use it.
claims.quote: const safeFile250bPng = pathFromHere('./safe-file-250b.png');
claims.note: Listed resources/file-upload: constants.ts, padded-pdf.ts, paths.ts, restricted-file-10b.txt, safe-file-100kb.jpg, safe-file-10kb.docx, safe-file-19kb.doc, safe-file-1kb.pdf, safe-file-25kb.xls, safe-file-500kb.jpeg, safe-file-50kb.xlsx. No PNG.

claims.statement: The hint text under the document type question and under the file input is not proven anywhere in this slice.
claims.note: The page object exposes a fieldHint(fieldId) helper and the specs never call it for this page; no spec in this part asserts a hint, an accessible description or any wording about which file types or sizes are allowed before an upload is tried.

claims.statement: The documents page also carries a plain "Continue" button, which the shared journey flows click to leave the page, but no test in this slice says when it is shown instead of the three save controls.
claims.note: Clicked only by the straight-through journey walks, which belong to another part; the specs in this part only ever use Save and add another, Save and continue or Save and return to overview.

claims.statement: No confirmation banner is proven after a document is added or removed: nothing in this slice asserts a success or important notification banner on the documents page.
claims.note: The shared page object offers successBanner and importantBanner locators; no spec in this part uses either. The only feedback these specs assert after a save is the row in the added-documents table.

claims.statement: Every refusal on the documents page is shown as a GOV.UK error summary headed "There is a problem", with a link per error.
The Overview task list names the documents step "Upload documents", placed after "Transport details" and before the consignment addresses, in both the air-or-sea and the overland orders.
claims.quote:
export const AIR_OR_SEA_OVERVIEW_TASKS = [
…
  'Transport details',
  'Upload documents',
  CONSIGNMENT_ADDRESSES,
  'Contact address for this consignment',
] as const;

claims.statement: Within the journey's Save-and-continue chain the documents page sits between the transport details page and the consignment addresses page, which is why Save and continue from it lands on Consignment addresses.
claims.quote:
const stops: SaveAndContinueStop[] = [
      this.animalsPages.importReason,
      this.animalsPages.consignmentDetails,
      this.animalsPages.animalIdentification,
      this.animalsPages.additionalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.arrivalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.transitedCountries,
      this.animalsPages.transporter,
      this.animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments,
      this.animalsPages.addresses,
      this.animalsPages.contactAddress,
    ];

claims.statement: Each upload the suite makes carries a unique document reference stamped with the moment it ran, so two runs never collide on a reference.
claims.note: mechanism: builds a unique document reference for each upload; it is test data, not a rule the service applies to a trader's own reference. Nothing in this slice proves whether two documents may share a reference.

claims.statement: A document row is found by its reference anywhere on the page, so the reference a trader types is shown in the list.

An infected upload is driven with the standard EICAR anti-virus test file sent as a PDF named eicar-virus-file.pdf with the application/pdf media type, so the refusal comes from the scanner rather than from a file-type check.
claims.quote:
/**
 * Returns the standard EICAR anti-virus test file as an in-memory PDF upload named `eicar-virus-file.pdf`.
 *
 * @see https://www.eicar.org/download-anti-malware-testfile/
 */
claims.note: The file's content is the published EICAR test string, held base64-encoded in the helper.

claims.statement: The 15-document cap is reached by saving each document with "Save and add another" and waiting for its row to read "Check completed" before the next, so each of the fifteen is scanned in turn rather than in one batch.
What happens when a trader tries to add a sixteenth document anyway — by posting past the shut add control — is not proven: the suite only checks that the control carries no upload address.
claims.note: The spec's comment says the claim would turn a sixteenth file away, but no test drives that path, so the refusal's wording and status are unproven here.

claims.statement: The second of the two file-upload timeouts, the one for the documents list becoming visible, is never used by any spec in this slice, so no test holds the page to a time for showing the list.
claims.quote: documentsListVisible: timeouts.medium,
claims.note: All eleven specs use only virusScanComplete.

claims.statement: Every spec in this part runs as a signed-in trader of one organisation: the suite hands each test its pages and journey already authenticated, signing in through the sign-in page when the session is cold.
Whether one organisation's trader can reach another organisation's uploaded document through its View file address is not proven in this slice.
claims.note: Both download checks fetch the View file address inside the same signed-in session that uploaded the file. The fixtures do offer a second-organisation API client, and no spec in this part uses it against a document download.

claims.statement: The notification reference numbers a test creates are recorded against the test run, so each run's report names the notifications it left behind.
claims.note: mechanism: collects the references a test created and writes them into the run's annotations; test housekeeping, not service behaviour.
